chapter: Faith, Paris life and later years
title: The locked door and the neighbour's burglary note
summary: A funny story of his wife locked out of the house, police breaking a window, and a note about the kitchen light left on in a neighbourhood with burglaries.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Well, a funny thing happened while I was away. I went to Belgium, you know, in the month of August, and took my wife, and I sent my kid to camp for the month of August. So I told my wife, well, I have this job teaching for six days, and then I have a concert, so you go with me to Belgium. Okay. So she returned a couple of days ahead of me because I had to go to a spa for a couple of days. So she said, 'Well, I'll go home and get the house in shape,' and so forth. So we have a lock on the door whereby when it's locked you can't get in or out. So she had lost her keys, but not thinking, we had new locks put on, but we didn't change the middle lock. So I locked the middle lock, thinking, as a habit I'd do that, you know.
So if anyone gets in they can't take anything out, you know?
But she arrived home and she remembered. She said, 'Oh, my God, Kenny locked the middle lock and I can't

get in the house." So she called a neighbor across the street and the neighbor called the police, so the police came and broke our bathroom window and went in through the window. But in the meantime, I had left the kitchen light burning, so evidently someone in the neighborhood put a note in my door and said, "It's useless to leave your kitchen light on because I can rob your house anyway. It won't stop me from robbing your house. But I know, Mr. Clarke --," et cetera, et cetera. Put the neighbor next door to me was robbed. Now, I said well somebody likes me in the neighborhood anyway. So that's how -- you know.

Someone in front of me, he was robbed and the guy next door to me was robbed. And they told me, said, "Inutile de laissez les lumieres dans le cuisin," because if I want to rob you I can rob you anyway. But I didn't leave the light on for that purpose. I just had forgotten to turn it out.
Because she had said we'll leave the icebox on because we'll only be gone a week, you know.
So she says we're protected by the . Well, the  is like the gangsters, you know.
So I figured it's worth living in a little neighborhood where I live, you know, because it's -- you know.
